definition: Chi-square refers to a statistical distribution formed from the sum of squared independent standard normal variables, and to tests that compare a calculated value with that distribution. In research, chi-square tests are commonly used to examine whether two or more population distributions differ.

provenance.scope: Source record D016009; pinned source text

While the packet supports that chi-square tests (the oldest of these tests) are used to detect whether two or more population distributions differ, the definition’s broader wording (“commonly used to examine whether two or more population distributions differ”) is not explicitly supported as stated.
“Commonly used” is not supported by the packet; the packet says only that the oldest chi-square tests are used to detect whether two or more population distributions differ.
